findings.text: [B]: the numeral 4 is tiny at the largest size and is just a speck at the smallest, so in one-color tint the icon reads as a night landscape and no longer says paint by numbers. Someone with low vision gets no clue about what the app does.

[D]: the 6 is big and stays clear at all three sizes, and the hills read as a filled region, so this is the most legible icon for low-vision users. The name 'Paint by Heart' sounds warm, but it suggests you need feeling or skill, which may not welcome someone who is just tapping numbers.
[C]: the moon's dark blotches crowd the 4, and at the smallest size the numeral merges into the craters, so the icon blurs into a textured circle.
[A]: the crescent outline survives at every size, but the 3 sits inside the curve and gets very small at the smallest size. Making it larger would fix that.
In the tinted rendering every icon is the same amber on brown, so contrast does all the work: [D] has the biggest light area and holds up best, while [B]'s thin stars disappear.
All four names sound natural when spoken in a sentence and nothing in them scolds the user. 'Moonlight' does hint at evening painting, but it doesn't exclude anyone.
